salary_details.details: Fixed Stipend for Cadet Training: Rs. 56,100 per month (starting pay in Level 10 of the Pay Matrix) throughout training at IMA Dehradun. On successful commissioning, the officer's pay is fixed in the first cell of Level 10; the training period is not treated as commissioned service, but arrears of admissible allowances for the training period are paid to cadets. Military Service Pay (MSP): Rs. 15,500 per month, fixed, for officers from Lieutenant to Brigadier rank. Dearness Allowance: Admissible at the same rates and conditions as applicable to civilian personnel, from time to time. Para Reserve Allowance: Rs. 2,625 per month. Technical Allowance: Tier-I – Rs. 3,000 per month; Tier-II – Rs. 4,500 per month. Field Area Allowances: Officers posted to Field Areas are eligible for allowances depending on rank and area of posting, ranging up to Rs. 42,500 (RH-Max) and including Siachen Allowance, High Altitude Allowance, Flying Allowance, Special Forces Allowance, and several other risk/hardship-linked allowances specified in the notification. These allowances apply strictly as per the laid-down qualification/eligibility conditions and are not admissible to everyone. Dress Allowance: Rs. 20,000 per year. Ration in Kind: In Peace and Field Areas. Transport Allowance (TPTA): For Pay Level 10 and above, Rs. 7,200 per month plus DA in Higher TPTA Cities (Hyderabad, Patna, Delhi, Ahmedabad, Surat, Bengaluru, Kochi, Kozhikode, Indore, Greater Mumbai, Nagpur, Pune, Jaipur, Chennai, Coimbatore, Ghaziabad, Kanpur, Lucknow, Kolkata), and Rs. 3,600 per month plus DA at other places. This is not admissible where Government transport is provided; officers in Pay Level 14 and above can opt for an official car or Rs. 15,750 per month plus DA; not admissible for months fully covered by leave; physically disabled service personnel are paid at double rate, minimum Rs. 2,250 plus DA per month. Children Education Allowance: Rs. 2,812.50 per month per child (per the Hindi text) / Rs. 2,250 per month per child (per the English text), for the two eldest surviving children, from pre-primary to Class 12. Reimbursement is once a year, after the financial year, on a certificate from the head of the institution. Hostel Subsidy: Rs. 6,750 per month per child, for the two eldest surviving children, from pre-primary to Class 12. Rates of Defence-specific allowances increase automatically by 25% each time Dearness Allowance rises by 50%, as per Government of India letter No. A-27012/02/2017-Est.(AL) dated 16 August 2017. | Pay, allowances and their rules/provisions are subject to revision from time to time. | Officer Cadets, while in receipt of stipend, are insured for Rs. 1.25 crore, as applicable to regular Army officers, with a monthly advance subscription of Rs. 12,500. Cadets invalided out by an Invaliding Medical Board (IMB) due to disability, and not entitled to any pension, are provided Rs. 25 lakh for 100% disability, proportionately reduced to Rs. 5 lakh for 20% disability; for disability below 20%, only an Ex-Gratia grant of Rs. 50,000 is paid. Disability due to alcoholism, drug addiction, or diseases of pre-enrolment origin does not qualify for this benefit. Officer Cadets withdrawn on disciplinary grounds, expelled as undesirable, or leaving the Academy voluntarily, are not eligible for the disability benefit or Ex-Gratia grant.

selection_process: Shortlisting of Applications: The Integrated HQ of MoD (Army) reserves the right to shortlist applications based on the vacancy-to-call-up ratio for each engineering stream

without assigning any reason. A cut-off is applied in each stream on the cumulative percentage of marks obtained up to the final semester/year. Percentages given by the college/university after applying their own CGPA-to-percentage formula are considered final; a candidate whose converted percentage falls below the cut-off should not report for SSB even if shortlisted as per the marks entered in the application. Allotment of Selection Centre and Dates: After shortlisting
candidates must log in to the website and select their SSB dates and centres
available on a first-come
first-served basis. The SSB centre and date
once selected
cannot be changed later

except that the Directorate General of Recruiting reserves the right to change a selected centre/date due to any exceptional circumstance. Conduct of SSB: Only shortlisted eligible candidates are called to one of the Selection Centres — Prayagraj (Uttar Pradesh)
Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh)
Bengaluru (Karnataka)

or Jalandhar (Punjab). The Call Up Letter is issued only through the candidate's registered email ID and SMS. Candidates go through a two-stage selection process; those who clear Stage-1 proceed to Stage-2

and those who fail Stage-1 are returned the same day. The SSB interview lasts a maximum of five days. Candidates recommended after Stage-2 undergo a medical examination. Joining Pre-Commission Training Academy (PCTA): Candidates recommended by the SSB and declared medically fit are issued a Joining Letter for training
in order of merit
subject to the number of vacancies available and meeting all eligibility criteria.
Candidates should check www.joinindianarmy.nic.in for the medical standards and procedures applicable to Officer Entry. The SSB medical examination is valid for 270 days

i.e. from the Special Medical Board (SMB) to the PCTA joining date. A candidate who has already undergone SSB medical examination (SMB/AMB/RMB) for the Army and been declared "Medically Fit" need not undergo it again for TGC-145

provided the gap between the medical (SMB) date and the course joining date (01 July 2027) is less than 270 days. Candidates already training in any Army PCTA need not undergo a fresh medical for TGC-145
even if this gap exceeds 270 days. Medical Board proceedings are confidential and are not divulged to anyone; the Directorate General of Recruiting has no role in any Medical Board.

Qualifying at the SSB interview does not by itself confirm final selection. The merit list is prepared stream/subject-wise on the marks obtained at the SSB interview. If candidates have equal SSB marks
the older candidate (by age) ranks higher. If SSB marks and age are both equal
the candidate with a higher percentage of marks in the qualifying degree is ranked higher; higher educational qualifications or previous performance play no role. Candidates within the merit list
within the stream-wise vacancies
and declared medically fit are issued Joining Letters for pre-commission training at IMA Dehradun
subject to meeting all eligibility criteria. If a candidate fails to report within 7 days of the reporting date in the Joining Letter
without the concerned Academy Adjutant's prior permission
the candidature is cancelled and a joining letter is issued to the next candidate in merit.

how_to_apply: Applications are accepted only online, on www.joinindianarmy.nic.in.
Click 'Officer Entry Apply/Login' and then 'Registration' (not required if already registered on the website).

Fill the online registration form after reading the instructions carefully. After registering, click 'Apply Online' under the Dashboard; a page 'Officers Selection Eligibility' will open. Click 'Apply' shown against Technical Graduate Course.

A page 'Application Form' will open. Read the instructions carefully and click 'Continue' to fill details under Personal information, Communication details, Education details, and details of previous SSB (if any). Click 'Save & Continue' before moving to the next segment.
After filling the last segment, you reach a 'Summary of your information' page, where you can check and edit entries already made. Only after confirming the details are correct, click 'Submit'.
Candidates must click 'Submit' each time they reopen the application to edit any detail.
After the online application finally closes on the last day, candidates must, 30 minutes later, take out two printed copies of their application bearing the Roll Number.

Aadhaar number and Matriculation certificate are mandatory for registration on the website. Candidates are advised to read the notification carefully before filling the online application, to avoid mistakes and rejection. Only one online application should be submitted; multiple applications from the same candidate will lead to cancellation of candidature, with no representation entertained.

No changes can be made to details submitted in the online application after its closure. CGPA/Grades must be converted into marks as per the formula adopted by the concerned university for filling 'Marks obtained in Graduation'; any discrepancy found at any stage of selection will lead to cancellation of candidature. The candidate's name, parents' names, and date of birth in the profile and online application must exactly match the Matriculation/Secondary School Examination Certificate (or equivalent) issued by the concerned Board of Education; any variation will lead to cancellation.

content_sections.heading: Indian Army TGC-145 Recruitment 2026 – Quick Summary
content_sections.text: Who is recruiting? Indian Army, through the Directorate General of Recruiting, for training at the Indian Military Academy (IMA), Dehradun. Which posts? 145th Technical Graduate Course (TGC-145) leading to Permanent Commission as a Lieutenant in the Indian Army. How many vacancies? 30 (tentative), across Civil, Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, Mechanical and Misc Engineering streams. Who can apply? Unmarried male candidates with a BE/B.Tech or M.Sc Computer Science in a notified engineering stream (or final-year candidates meeting the conditions below), aged 20 to 27 years as on 01 July 2027. Application start date: 30 September 2026, 1500 Hrs. Last date: 29 October 2026, 1500 Hrs. Application mode: Online only, at www.joinindianarmy.nic.in. Training location: Indian Military Academy (IMA), Dehradun. SSB interviews are held at Prayagraj (UP), Bhopal (MP), Bengaluru (Karnataka) or Jalandhar (Punjab).

content_sections.heading: Indian Army TGC-145 Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: A candidate must be either: (i) a citizen of India, or (ii) a subject of Nepal, or (iii) a person of Indian origin who has migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, or the East African countries of Kenya, Uganda, the United Republic of Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, Ethiopia or Vietnam, with the intention of permanently settling in India. Candidates in categories (ii) and (iii) must have a certificate of eligibility issued by the Government of India, except Gorkha subjects of Nepal, for whom this certificate is not necessary. Where required, this certificate must be attached with the application. Only unmarried male candidates are eligible to apply.

content_sections.heading: Type of Commission, Seniority and Training
content_sections.text: Grant of Commission: Selected candidates are granted a Short Service Commission on probation in the rank of Lieutenant, from the date of course commencement or the date of reporting at IMA Dehradun, whichever is later. Permanent Commission: On successful completion of training, cadets are granted Permanent Commission in the Army in the rank of Lieutenant. Ante Date Seniority: Engineering Graduates of TGC entry are granted one year of ante-date seniority from the date of commission, in the rank of Lieutenant, for seniority, promotion and pay increment purposes. Induction in IMA: Selected candidates are detailed for training at IMA Dehradun according to their position in the final order of merit (stream-wise), up to the number of available vacancies. Duration of training is about 12 months. Marriage During Training: Candidates are not allowed to marry during training, nor to live with parents/guardians. A candidate who marries during training is discharged and is liable to refund all government expenditure on him; a candidate who marries after applying (even if successful in the SSB and medical) is not inducted for training, and the candidature is cancelled. Cost of Training: Training at IMA Dehradun is at government expense. If an Officer Cadet is withdrawn from the Academy for reasons other than medical grounds or reasons beyond his control, he is liable to refund the cost of training at Rs. 20,481.96 per week (tentative; actual cost calculated at the time of withdrawal/resignation), as per MoD letter No. 16(1)/2017-D(GS.II) dated 15 March 2022, with an annual increment of 8%. The cost of training borne by the State is recovered from candidates withdrawing for personal reasons. Allocation of Arms/Services: The final allocation of Arms/Services is made prior to the Officer Cadets' passing out from IMA, at the sole discretion of the Integrated HQ of the Ministry of Defence (Army). No representation on this allocation is entertained.

The candidate's name, parents' names, and date of birth in the profile and online application must exactly match the Matriculation/Secondary School Examination Certificate (or equivalent) issued by the concerned Board of Education; any variation will lead to cancellation.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required at the SSB (Selection Centre)
content_sections.text: Self-attested copies of the following documents, along with their originals, must be carried to the Selection Centre. DIGILOCKER certificates will not be accepted in place of original certificates. One printout of the application, duly signed and affixed with a self-attested photograph. Matriculation/Secondary School Examination certificate (or equivalent) and marksheet issued by the concerned Board of Education, as proof of date of birth, candidate's name and parents' names (no other document such as admit card/marksheet/transfer certificate is acceptable). If parents' names are not mentioned on this certificate, the candidate must produce a Government of India/State Government document (PAN card, Aadhaar Card, Passport, Driving Licence, etc.) for verification, and the names in the online application must match this document exactly. 12th class marksheet and certificate, or equivalent certificate/Diploma marksheet and certificate (for Diploma holders). Engineering Degree/Provisional Degree issued by the recognised university (the Provisional Degree must not be more than six months old at the time of joining the Academy). Marksheets of all semesters/years. Certificate from the Controller of Examination/Registrar of the concerned university regarding the CGPA/Grades-to-marks conversion formula. For final-year candidates: a certificate from the Controller of Exam/Registrar/Dean/Principal regarding the cumulative percentage of marks up to the relevant semester/year, and a certificate from the Principal/Head of the Institution confirming the candidate is in the final year with the result to be declared by 01 July 2027, plus a declaration to submit proof of passing by 01 July 2027 to the Directorate General of Recruiting. Documents related to civil/police verification. A candidate who does not carry the above documents for the SSB interview will have their candidature cancelled and be returned. All certificates must be carried in original for verification; originals are returned after verification at the Service Selection Board itself. If a school/college issues only e-certificates through DIGILOCKER (no hard copy), a certificate to this effect must be obtained from the school/college, along with a duly authenticated colour printout of the e-certificate.

content_sections.heading: Other Important Conditions
content_sections.text: Disclosure of Material Information: Candidates must disclose all material information in their application/at the SSB, including any previous training in a training academy, release, withdrawal, resignation or dismissal from it, medical invalidment/unfitness declared by a competent authority, and any other information bearing on eligibility or suitability for commission. Suppression of material information can lead to cancellation of candidature at any stage up to grant of commission, or thereafter. Travelling Allowance: Candidates appearing for the SSB interview for the first time for a particular type of commission are entitled to AC-III Tier railway fare (or bus fare with reservation-cum-sleeper charges) to and fro, within Indian limits. Candidates reapplying for the same type of commission are not entitled to this allowance on any subsequent occasion. Change of Interview Date/Centre: Once the SSB date is selected, no request for a change of date/centre will be entertained or replied to. Any ambiguity, false information, or concealment of information detected in certificates/documents/the online application will result in cancellation of candidature at any stage of selection and thereafter. A candidate must never have been debarred from appearing in any examination by the UPSC, and must never have been arrested or convicted by a criminal court or involved in any case; if such an issue comes to notice during selection or pre-commission training, the candidature/cadetship is liable to cancellation/withdrawal by the Integrated HQ of MoD (Army). Candidates withdrawn from the NDA, IMA, OTA, Naval Academy, Air Force Academy, or any Service Training Academy on disciplinary grounds are not eligible to apply. Candidates serving in the Armed Forces must inform their Commanding Officer in writing that they have applied, and their application (countersigned by the Commanding Officer) must be carried to the SSB along with the other documents. For queries on centre allotment, interview dates, merit list, joining instructions or other information, candidates should check www.joinindianarmy.nic.in; queries are answered only through the 'Feedback/Query' option on the website, and only those received up to 3 days before the closing of the online application will be entertained. On joining the Army, certain personal restrictions apply under Article 33 of the Constitution of India, as promulgated in the Army Act and Army Rules from time to time.

faq.question: Q1. What is Indian Army TGC-145 Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It is the recruitment of unmarried male Engineering Graduates for the 145th Technical Graduate Course, commencing July 2027 at the Indian Military Academy (IMA), Dehradun, leading to Permanent Commission in the Indian Army.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available in TGC-145?
faq.answer: There are 30 tentative vacancies: Civil-08, Computer Science-06, Electrical-02, Electronics-06, Mechanical-06, and Misc Engineering Streams-02.

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply for TGC-145?
faq.answer: The online application closes on 29 October 2026 at 1500 Hrs. It opened on 30 September 2026 at 1500 Hrs.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for TGC-145?
faq.answer: Candidates must be 20 to 27 years old as on 01 July 2027, i.e. born between 01 July 2000 and 30 June 2007.

faq.question: Q5. What is the application fee for TGC-145?
faq.answer: The application fee is not specified in the notification.

faq.question: Q6. How can I apply online for TGC-145?
faq.answer: Register and apply at www.joinindianarmy.nic.in under 'Officer Entry Apply/Login', fill the application form across the personal, communication, and education sections, and submit before 29 October 2026, 1500 Hrs. Aadhaar and Matriculation certificate are mandatory for registration.

faq.question: Q7. What is the selection process for TGC-145?
faq.answer: Applications are shortlisted stream-wise on cumulative percentage of marks, followed by a two-stage SSB interview (up to 5 days) at Prayagraj, Bhopal, Bengaluru or Jalandhar, then a medical examination, and a stream-wise merit list based on SSB marks.

faq.question: Q8. What is the stipend and pay for TGC-145 cadets and officers?
faq.answer: Cadets receive a fixed stipend of Rs. 56,100 per month during training at IMA. On commissioning, pay starts at Level 10 (Rs. 56,100–1,77,500) for a Lieutenant, plus Military Service Pay of Rs. 15,500 per month and other allowances as applicable. Cadets receive a fixed stipend of Rs. 56,100 per month during training at IMA. On commissioning, pay starts at Level 10 (Rs. 56,100–1,77,500) for a Lieutenant, plus Military Service Pay of Rs. 15,500 per month and other allowances as applicable.
